input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Deepen flagship 8 quick-pick-survey, item (r): get the rank page in front of people with a data-backed answer page

errors.what: Tried a stop rule (stop once every pair answered once with no cycle) for short lists
errors.result: Measured on 40 simulated people a cell: fired only at 4 options (2-3 picks saved, -0.025 Spearman on close calls) because nextPair re-asks neighbours rather than covering every pair; dropped before commit

errors.what: First draft of the answer page claimed a consistent person always needs more than log2(n!) picks
errors.result: False from 40 options (150 vs 160; 229 vs 273 at 60) because the stop is at 90% settled, not exact; the sentence is now computed from the rows

errors.what: First draft said 'adaptive wins' on long lists
errors.result: Every pair once is more accurate from about 15 options (0.97 vs 0.92 at 40) at 4x the questions; page now states both

doc_friction.issue: The hook that blocks pkill -f also blocks a bracketed pattern when the same word appears elsewhere in the command line (e.g. a later node scripts/picks-needed.mjs); split into two calls. CLAUDE.md mentions bracketing but not this.

The status line's 'Lists of n usually take n log2 n to 1.5 n log2 n picks' was never measured; it was low for close-call answerers (15 options: said 59-88, measured 104). Replaced with measured numbers.

deviations.why: Took flagship item (r) (distribution) with a measurement-backed answer page rather than an algorithm item, because (r) is listed most valuable first and the page needed real data the repo did not have
deviations.did: Measured picks-to-stop on the ranker's own loop at 4-60 options, generated the answer page and the status line from the rows
deviations.result: Page and status line ship with every number computed from docs/picks-needed-2026-11-14.jsonl

deviations.why: Did not wait for the 60-option close-call cell (projected 45+ more minutes)
deviations.did: Shipped tables to 50 options; status line for >50 says 'the longest measured' instead of extrapolating
deviations.result: No unmeasured number on the page

goal: Get the free rank page in front of people searching how many pairwise comparisons ranking a list needs, with measured answers
notes: Verification: node --test site/picks-page.test.mjs site/use-pages.test.mjs site/rank-core.test.mjs 47 pass; Playwright at 390 px: answer page scrollWidth 390, ranker status line shows measured picks, no console errors; venture-preflight clean; PR CI 23 check runs green before the final data commit. The 50 and 60-option close-call cells take 30-60 min each (prior search every pick up to a 565-709 cap). Final: the 60-option close-call cell was stopped unfinished after 50 min (50-option cell took 37 min); the page table stops at 50 and the status line labels 50 as the longest measured for longer lists. Staleness test checked red on a hand-edited number, green restored.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: simulation harness, generated answer page with tests, write-ups: about a day for a data engineer

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
